criteria: Investigate cross-thread communication and playback ownership in actual ChatGPT MCP Apps instances, documenting platform and scope limits.
Within the supported scope, starting playback in one Dial instance stops or pauses any previously playing Dial instance so two streams do not remain audible together.
Play and Pause behavior in a second thread is defined explicitly, including whether its controls operate the active playback or transfer ownership.
Playback ownership and visible player state recover predictably after rapid interactions, closed or remounted instances, and unavailable coordination.
Automated coordination tests and separate actual two-thread ChatGPT playback evidence cover the approved behavior.

objective: Investigate and define a single active playback experience across Dial instances in different ChatGPT threads; prevent overlapping audio and make Play/Pause behavior clear.

reports.complexity: Moderate-to-high. A local coordination protocol is modest if ChatGPT provides same-origin, same-partition sibling instances, but exclusive ownership, races, stale-owner recovery, and observable state require a protocol rather than a simple broadcast. If that prerequisite fails, a server design needs user identity, shared durable/low-latency state, authorization and connection lifecycle work, beyond current scope.
evidence: MCP Apps render UI resources in sandboxed iframes, communicating with their host through a defined protocol; teardown/remount is part of lifecycle. The MCP Apps overview describes no host DOM/cookie/storage access and a controlled postMessage channel. Source: https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/documents/overview.html (official platform protocol documentation). Implication: Sibling Dial iframes do not have a documented direct host-provided cross-thread control API. Their common origin and lifecycle are host implementation details unless observed or explicitly guaranteed.

BroadcastChannel communicates between contexts on the same origin and same storage partition; an embedded third-party context can be partitioned away from a first-party context even where URL origins match. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Broadcast_Channel_API (browser API documentation). Implication: BroadcastChannel is a plausible low-latency same-browser/device option only if both ChatGPT thread iframes receive a compatible shared origin and partition. It is not evidence that ChatGPT currently provides that arrangement.

Browser state APIs including localStorage, IndexedDB, BroadcastChannel, Shared Workers and Service Workers are generally partitioned by top-level site; third-party embeds generally cannot access state under another top-level site. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Privacy/Guides/State_Partitioning (browser privacy documentation). Implication: Storage-based locks or service-worker ownership are subject to the same host partition question and cannot establish cross-device coordination.

OpenAI ChatGPT UI docs say the UI runs in an isolated iframe and browser storage is not a reliable cross-device or cross-session data layer; durable cross-session state should be server-side and authenticated. Source: https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui (official OpenAI documentation). Implication: Do not use localStorage as a product guarantee across threads/sessions/devices. A server-owned coordination service would need a stable authenticated user identity and account mapping, which this request and current server do not provide.

CSP resourceDomains includes media and connectDomains governs fetch/XHR/WebSocket requests for MCP UI resources. Source: https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/interfaces/app.McpUiResourceCsp.html (official MCP Apps protocol documentation). Implication: A server/WebSocket coordination experiment would require permitted CSP connectDomains and a host-supported network path; current Dial CSP has no connectDomains.

Current Dial player state is local to the iframe, and server transport is created sessionless per request without a shared coordination store or user identity. Source: src/player-controller.ts; src/player.ts; src/server.ts (repository inspection) (observed source code). Implication: No present in-repo mechanism can identify the other thread's stream or issue a direct pause to its audio element. The server cannot directly pause media being played by another iframe.
open_questions: Host experiment: in the same ChatGPT browser profile/device, open the Dial player in two distinct threads concurrently. Inspect each iframe's effective origin and probe whether a uniquely named BroadcastChannel message from one is received by the other; repeat after remount, closing the active thread, backgrounding it, and with rapid simultaneous Play. Record browser/platform, timestamp, whether both iframes coexist, origin/partition observations available to the tester, and observed message/ack timing. Do not infer support from local browser tests.

If same-partition delivery works, run a small host feasibility probe for an acknowledgment/ownership exchange under background throttling and teardown; confirm whether Web Locks or another atomic primitive is exposed in that same partition before specifying exclusivity. A BroadcastChannel-only success proves delivery, not race-free single ownership.

Product decision for Spec/owner: should a Play in the second thread take ownership and stop the first stream, or should it refuse playback while another instance owns it? The request favors preventing overlap but does not choose transfer versus refusal.

Product decision for Spec/owner: should Pause in an idle second player pause the active first player's stream, or only control the local player? Cross-instance Pause requires an explicit remote-control protocol and clearer active-owner UI; local no-op is simplest if not authorized.

Confirm intended support boundary after feasibility evidence: same browser profile/device only, or an explicitly broader scope that would require identity-backed server coordination. No current evidence supports the broader scope.
reports.recommendation_reason: The work requires an approval-bound PRODUCT.md/TECH.md because user-visible transfer/refusal and remote Pause semantics remain undecided, and feasibility depends on an unverified host-origin/storage-partition condition. First capture the focused actual two-thread ChatGPT probe described above. If it confirms same-partition messaging and an acceptable arbitration primitive, Spec the smallest local same-device design, explicit unsupported-coordination behavior, remount/stale-owner/race recovery, and separate automated plus host evidence. If it fails, return to Foreman/owner with that result and decide whether to park the request or explicitly authorize identity-backed server coordination; do not silently add accounts, cross-device support, or deployment.
relevant_code: src/player-controller.ts: Each rendered UI instance independently owns its HTMLAudioElement and local wanted/attempt/player state; Play/Pause only call that instance's audio.play()/pause(). No cross-instance coordination exists.
src/player.ts: Creates one player controller per rendered iframe; current app bridge is used for reporting a station click only.

src/server.ts: MCP HTTP handler creates a fresh McpServer and sessionless StreamableHTTPServerTransport per request. Existing server exposes no shared playback registry, identity, or coordination endpoint; CSP currently allows media origins and no connectDomains.
public/player.html: Contains the per-instance audio element; source is served as MCP UI resource and rendered by the host.

factory/work-items/DIAL-003/REQUEST.md: Request explicitly says actual ChatGPT iframe/origin/lifecycle constraints are unresolved, acceptance criteria are provisional, and no implementation has started.
risks: BroadcastChannel messages are transient and do not themselves provide durable ownership, acknowledgments, or a linearizable lock; simultaneous Play actions can race unless a stronger arbitration mechanism is validated and specified.

The sandbox host may assign opaque or per-resource/per-instance origins, or separate storage partitions between threads; in that case BroadcastChannel/localStorage/Web Locks/worker approaches may fail silently or be scoped too narrowly.

Browser scheduling, throttled/background iframes, teardown, and missed messages can leave a stale owner or allow overlap. A second instance cannot truthfully display the first instance's live state without successful coordination and freshness semantics.

A server-mediated solution could coordinate only if instances can be associated with the same authorized user and reliably reach the same service. Current transport is sessionless per request and carries no documented user identity; introducing accounts/deployment is outside this triage scope.

Polling a server/tool would add latency and may fail while a view is backgrounded; an always-open WebSocket would need CSP, authentication, operational availability, and reconnect/ownership semantics.
A local-browser solution cannot coordinate between devices or distinct browser profiles. Cross-device behavior is not inferred from the user's separate-thread request.
reports.scope: Read-only feasibility and architecture triage for preventing overlapping playback between Dial MCP App instances opened in separate ChatGPT threads. Assessment covers browser communication primitives, host sandbox/origin/storage constraints, present server shape, and the host experiment needed before design approval. It does not assume multiple-device scope and does not claim any ChatGPT host experiment was run.
